before.label: English
before.title: A World of Love Is Slipping Away
stanzas: A world of love is slipping away,
I am heading towards ruin.
All faces are unfamiliar,
neither words nor a smile upon the lips.
The poem I wrote about the eyes is blurred now;
a world of distrust keeps growing.
Wiped clean each day, the mirror seeks a new face.
The river water flows on.
I look at my face,
but this is not the same water,
and the face is different too.
I am a mountain, steadfast in wisdom,
standing still.
They climb over me to touch the summit;
I keep all their footprints safe.
The birds’ wings, their flights,
the daily search for newer skies, and
the sorrow of their moving away from me
weigh upon me.
If silence is a forest, it surrounds me;
if the city is a clamour, it is moving away from me.
I have put all the faces in an album.
Now and then, I look at them,
then put it back inside the trunk.
I wonder whether the faces in the album
must be talking to one another inside the trunk!
How is it that they never grow older,
remaining still?
How, without saying anything to anyone,
do they converse?
A lifetime passes in a single shirt.
Time stands still, no questions, no answers;
everyone is without an answer.
They understand one another well;
emotion, happiness and sorrow
are entangled in one particular moment.
Outside, darkness and light play hide-and-seek.
Outside, weapons change hands.
Outside, the murderous moon.
Outside, false smiles, false love,
the life of a fish covered in ice.
Outside, the market, the crowd, the buzzing flies.
Can anyone, by remembering another,
keep them alive in memory?
Do termites eat the wooden chest of love?
The figures who visit my dreams at night
vanish at the break of dawn.
I wait for another night,
another dream,
another mirror, and
a restless river flowing past.
Tikrapada, Post/District Balangir, 767001

before.label: English
before.title: Renewed
stanzas: Under the curse of all your sins,
one day you will fall to earth,
buried beneath the heap of your downfall.
Not a character on the pages of history,
you will remain a stain,
with a putrid smell.
The sandstorm of time will cover
all your footprints;
the wind will carry away
the handful of ash from your last remaining bone.
The sky will look clear that day,
as though it has just defeated
the demon of dark clouds in a wrestling match.
All those chicks of your dreams,
for whose eyes to open one day
you show so much arrogance—
one day they will become blind death’s food.
It will crumble into particles,
your artificial tower, one day.
One day your royal throne will stand empty,
the line of servants and slaves will perish.
The ceremonial fans and fly-whisks will taste dust;
no trace of you will remain—
songs of victory, inscriptions,
memories, honours.
Declaring one day
all the suffering you cause unbearable,
the earth will shake herself free.
In a deluge she will wash away
all her wounds and bloodstains.
One day, amid a new chorus of voices,
she will proclaim—
I am “Renewed.”

before.label: हिन्दी
before.title: आधा पागल
stanzas: मैं मनुष्य होकर भी
मनुष्यों को डरा देता हूँ।
बोलते-बोलते सारे घाव मुखर हो उठते हैं।
झुकी पलकों वाली आँखें,
सो गए कान,
नींद के कीचड़ से उठ नहीं पाते
यातना के विकराल उजले उत्सव तक।
आँसुओं से भरे बादल की
टूटी पुकार लौटने से पहले,
आदिम पीड़ा का उपला जलने से पहले,
वे समय के ढेले खोज लाते हैं
मुझ पर फेंकने को।
मेरा पिता नहीं है, इसलिए
मेरी सिसकियों से पृथ्वी की नींद नहीं टूटती।
कुछ लोग पास बैठ जाते हैं,
कंधे पर विश्वास रख देते हैं,
एक चाँद हरसिंगार की छाती पर आँसू बहाता है,
अचानक।
कुल्हाड़ी की चोट खाई बड़ी डाल जैसे दिखते हैं
मेरे सारे दिन।
रास्ते से आते-जाते परिचित कहते हैं:
मैं उदास खेत में शरद की धान की बाली हूँ,
मैं एक शहरी आधा पागल हूँ
जो काटता रहता है
अपनी डाल, तना, जड़ें,
जब तक पहचान न लूँ: मेरा बीज, मेरी मिट्टी,
मेरा जन्म, मेरी मृत्यु।
एरोड्रोम एरिया, भुवनेश्वर ७५१०२०

before.label: English
before.title: Half-Mad
stanzas: Though I am human,
I frighten other humans.
As I speak, all the wounds grow vocal.
Eyes with lowered lids,
ears that have fallen asleep,
cannot rise from the mire of slumber
to pain’s fierce, radiant festival.
Before the torn cry
of the tear-laden cloud returns,
before the dung-cake of primal grief catches fire,
they find clods of time
to fling at me.
Because I have no father,
my sobbing does not wake the earth.
Some sit beside me,
place their trust upon my shoulder;
a moon sheds tears on the night-jasmine’s breast,
suddenly.
Like a grown branch struck by an axe
my days appear.
An acquaintance passing on the road says:
I am an autumn ear of rice in a desolate field,
I am an urban half-mad man
who keeps hacking away
his own branches, base and roots,
until I recognise: my seed, my soil,
my birth, my death.
Aerodrome Area, Bhubaneswar 751020

before.label: English
before.title: The One Who Writes Poetry
stanzas: The fragrance of a flower is poetry.
On the canvas of the sky’s blue curtain
poetry can be written.
In the labourer’s dripping sweat
poetry flows, rich with its scent.
Can poetry truly be written?
Can the one who writes it
name themselves a poet?
In the koel’s call
many an afternoon
feels fresh, not weary.
The scent of mango blossom,
coated with a layer of flying dust,
when it draws near me,
a half-written poem,
bearing a raw wound,
strikes against my windowsill.
In the ink of the pen
poetry rubs its body.
All the unruly words,
dressed as an illusory beloved,
have to be coaxed;
one must catch
fireflies in daylight.
Poetry is now waste paper in the scrap dealer’s shop.
Poetry, in a chamber where corpses are kept,
is about to turn to ice.
Clusters upon clusters of poems,
in the dreadful roar of the marketplaces,
have fallen silent.
The one who writes poetry?
Neither became a poet
nor could drag themselves free
of poetry’s lanes and alleys.
How much more can be crammed into an overstuffed sack?
If one sits down to write poetry, will it become poetry?
